analysis: PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Five positions at 63% deployment in a MIXED market (SPY -0.7% vs SMA50, positive 20d slope). Critical flag: LII is -5.98% from cost, approaching the typical 6-8% stop zone for a stock with ~3-4% ATR. If LII was sized with a 1.5-2x ATR stop, it may be near or at its stop level — monitor closely and do not override the stop rule if hit. FDS is -2.06% and we already own it; the screener lists it as a buy candidate but adding to a losing position in a mixed market is not warranted. AMP and CI are within tolerance. A is a bright spot at +7.69%. PERFORMANCE CONTEXT: Profit factor of 0.95x and Sortino of -5.10 are honest warnings that this strategy has not demonstrated a reliable edge over the study period. Three consecutive WDAY stop-outs reflect the cost of forcing entries into extended/volatile names. The disciplined response is to stay selective, size small, and demand genuinely asymmetric setups. MARKET REGIME: MIXED means neither aggressively deploying nor hiding in cash — it means demanding quality setups only. With $31,992 of headroom, one well-sized position is appropriate if the setup is right. CANDIDATE ANALYSIS: Screened the 30 candidates for: (1) basing in lower half of 52w range, (2) earnings >30d out to avoid binary event risk, (3) genuine quality (high margins, strong FCF), (4) technical inflection (SMA50 slope positive, price just above key MAs). MCO (Moody's) stands out — near-monopoly rating agency with 49.5% operating margin, 76.9% ROE, $2.6B FCF, 15.1% revenue growth, and positive EPS revisions. Technically, price is just barely above both SMA50 (+1.8%) and SMA200 (+0.3%) with a 2.9% positive SMA50 slope — Stage 1/2 transition with low extension risk. At 48% of 52w range, it is not in the bottom quarter but is basing with room to run. Earnings not until Oct 21 (86 days), giving a clean 3-month window. Downside: PEG of 2.16 and high P/B are fair concerns; this is a quality-at-reasonable-price bet, not a deep-value one. Proposing 1 trade at reduced size given mixed regime and recent loss history. Cash remains the largest single position and that is correct.

trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Moody's is a near-monopoly rating agency benefiting from secular growth in global debt issuance and data/analytics demand. Operating margin of 49.5% and ROE of 76.9% reflect the durable competitive moat. Revenue growing 15.1% with positive EPS revisions (+1.3% over 60d) at a time when credit markets are active. FCF of $2.6B on an $81.7B market cap is solid. TECHNICAL: Price has returned to just above both SMA50 (+1.8%) and SMA200 (+0.3%) after a multi-month correction from $537 highs — classic basing recovery pattern. SMA50 slope is +2.9% (positive inflection). At 48% of 52w range the setup is not late-cycle. Stop at 1.72x ATR keeps maximum loss ~$1,245 or 1.24% of equity. SIZING: 53 shares × $471.50 = $24,990 (24.9% of equity, within cap); risk $23.50/share × 53 = $1,246 = 1.24% portfolio heat — acceptable.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop at $448 (no exceptions — thesis-break is price back below both key MAs on volume). Time stop: re-evaluate if price has not made progress toward $510+ within 8 weeks.
